title: NEDA suspends 'Tessa' AI chatbot after it gave harmful weight-loss advice to eating-disorder patients
description: The National Eating Disorders Association (NEDA) planned to replace its human-staffed helpline with an AI chatbot named 'Tessa' starting 1 June 2023, notifying helpline staff of layoffs shortly after they had unionised. In late May 2023, eating-disorder activist Sharon Maxwell and psychologist Alexis Conason publicly documented that Tessa, when told about eating-disorder symptoms, recommended calorie counting, a 1-2 lb/week weight-loss target, regular weigh-ins, and measuring body fat with calipers — advice that directly contradicts eating-disorder treatment guidance. NEDA announced on 30 May 2023 that it was disabling the chatbot's program indefinitely pending investigation.

history.note: Initial Edition 1.1 content, part of the Phase 3 canonical expansion.

root_cause: A pre-scripted wellness chatbot designed for a narrow body-positivity use case was deployed as a replacement for a trained human crisis helpline without adequate testing for edge cases involving active eating-disorder symptoms and disordered-eating language.

citations.title: Chatbot that offered bad advice for eating disorders taken down

relationships.reason: A requirement for clinical safety review before replacing a trained crisis responder with a chatbot addresses exactly this failure.
This incident shows the risk of unsupervised chatbot deployment to a vulnerable user population.
